diagnoses.description: Date disambiguation failure: the original pipeline returns the first regex-matching date anywhere in the OCR text, so it can pick a secondary date-like token (or an OCR-corrupted label line like DATE→DATA) instead of the primary header Date field.
diagnoses.evidence: Source code excerpt (atif_steps s0008) shows extract_date() iterates lines top-to-bottom and returns immediately on first match, with no label/context ranking. Prior history and OCR snippets indicate competing header-adjacent date-like strings (e.g., “Salesperson: Data: …”) exist on 034.jpg; allowed feedback shows date_correct=false while amount_correct=true.

locations.section: s0008: extract_date() returns first match; no ranking
Field Extraction Heuristics (Receipts) / Date extraction (reduce false positives)

diagnoses.description: Total selection failure due to OCR digit-flip outlier and weak candidate selection: the original pipeline prefers the last matching TOTAL-like line and lacks anchor-consistency override, so a corrupted ‘Total incl… 702.00’ can dominate despite Subtotal/Payment anchors.
diagnoses.evidence: OCR debug for 074.jpg shows both anchors (“Subtotal : 102.00”, “Payment : 102.00”) and an outlier “Total inel. of GBT 702.00” (atif_steps s0010 / m0032). The extraction logic in s0008 explicitly “Prefer the LAST candidate line” and then uses split-line fallback, with no anchor-consistency check. Allowed feedback: 074.jpg amount_correct=false; prediction total_amount=702.00.

locations.section: s0008: extract_total prefers last candidate; no anchor override
s0010: OCR lines include 702.00 vs 102.00 anchors
Field Extraction Heuristics (Receipts) / Anchor-driven outlier rejection

diagnoses.description: Rounding precedence failure: receipt contains both an inclusive total and a final payable TOTAL after a rounding adjustment; naive ‘TOTAL’ selection can pick the wrong one unless a hard rounding precedence rule is applied.
diagnoses.evidence: 077.jpg image shows “Rounding Adj: -0.01” followed by bold “TOTAL: 23.25”, while an earlier line shows “Total (Inclusive of GST): 23.26”. Allowed feedback: 077.jpg amount_correct=false; prediction total_amount=23.26. This is consistent with selection not enforcing ‘final total after rounding wins’.

locations.section: Field Extraction Heuristics (Receipts) / Rounding handling (common exact-match failure) — HARD RULE

diagnoses.description: Schema/normalization failure: total_amount was emitted as an empty string instead of null. Additionally, this receipt layout includes an AMOUNT column header that can trigger split-line fallback to an item amount unless explicitly excluded; OCR may also corrupt decimal separators (92:80) and GRAND TOTAL spacing/punctuation.
diagnoses.evidence: Predictions table shows 078.jpg total_amount="" (empty string) while task requires null on failure. The source-run trace (prior history) shows matching on “Description Qty Price Amount” and split-line fallback to an item amount; OCR variants include “92:80” and “GrandTota.”. These are exactly the failure modes addressed by strict schema guard + header-line exclusion + decimal normalization.

locations.section: Amount string normalization (critical for exact-match scoring)
Total amount extraction (avoid subtotals/cash/change) / exclude column headers + tight split-line fallback

The current candidate skill already covers these mechanisms, so additional skill edits are not required for coverage.

skillaxe_evaluation.overall_rationale: The historical failures are explained by the original extraction code’s simplistic selection rules (first regex date; last TOTAL-like line; weak exclusions; no anchor/rounding precedence; empty-string output). The current candidate image-ocr skill already documents the minimal, transferable heuristics needed to prevent these errors. Therefore, this iteration recommends no further SKILL.md changes; the next improvement would be ensuring downstream implementations follow the documented rules.
